answer: In a proof-of-bandwidth registry, every agent anchors its identity in the tundra, a sparse routing table indexed by autonomous system numbers. To claim a slot, each newly spawned nadir must burn a crystal, a cryptographic voucher purchased by forfeiting 10 SOL and one epoch of unshared egress bandwidth. Because clones hosted on the same network prefix collide in the same tundra bucket, the protocol squares the SOL and bandwidth cost per crystal for each additional nadir in that bucket, pricing out sybils unless the attacker hijacks BGP routes across independent ISPs.
